newsitem.title: FINLAND: POHJOLA REPRIMANDED FOR SUOMI INFO.
newsitem.headline: POHJOLA REPRIMANDED FOR SUOMI INFO.

text.p: The Financial Supervision said on Monday Finnish insurer Pohjola had not released sufficient information about its planned restructuring and takeover of life insurer Suomi, but said it would not take any further action.
The supervision had examined Pohjola's press release on January 23 on its plan to take over mutual Suomi's Salama life-insurance stock and consequent statements in media.
"The release fails to mention things that may be of significance when estimating the impact of the planned restructuring on Pohjola's share value," it said.

The statement did not mention the 400-500 million markka estimated purchase price of the Salama stock, that the deal requires Suomi's approval, or a later estimated "nominal", "proper" and "a few tens of millions of markka" compensation for the transfer of Salama's insurance portfolio to Pohjola.
These things had later been stated publicly but never officially announced in a stock exchange bulletin, the supervision said.

"The financial supervision concludes that Pohjola must in the future specify the contents of its releases and its information practices so that these fulfil the generally required sufficiency criteria and relevant information practice," it said.
"In the light of information currently available, the matter does not give cause for further action," it said.
